about.title: About LandShield BD
about.intro: A civic-tech prototype built on synthetic data. It supports human reviewers and never makes a legal determination.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.body: LandShield BD shows how digital record organisation, consistency checks and transparent risk indicators could help people and reviewers examine land records before a transaction.

limits.title: Limitations
limits.l1: It is a prototype and has not been tested on real records.
limits.l2: Text extraction can be wrong; every document needs human review.
limits.l3: Risk indicators point to potential inconsistencies and can be false alarms.
limits.l4: It does not cover every kind of land record or every legal situation.

faraid.disclaimer: Guidance only, not a legal ruling. It follows Hanafi rules for common heirs. Other religions' succession laws differ; grandparents, grandchildren, half-siblings, wills and missing persons are not covered. Ask a lawyer.

errors.SPOUSE_BOTH: A husband and wives cannot both be heirs of the same person.
errors.COUNT_RANGE: Counts must be whole numbers from 0 to 30.

notes.awl: The fixed shares added up to more than the whole, so every share was reduced in proportion (awl).
notes.radd: There was no residuary heir, so the remainder returned to the sharers other than a spouse (radd).
notes.umar: Mother takes one third of what remains after the spouse (the two-parents-and-spouse rule).
notes.excluded: Siblings are excluded by a son or the father.
notes.leftover: Part of the estate is not assigned to any listed heir. Other relatives or the state may be entitled.
notes.scope: Not covered: grandparents, grandchildren, half-siblings, wills, missing persons, other religions.
notes.partition: Sharing the plot needs a registered partition deed and a mutation.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.purpose: Short answers about what LandShield BD does and does not do.

q1.a: A demonstration web app that shows how digital land-record checks, document verification and risk indicators could work. It runs on synthetic sample data.

q2.q: Is this an official government service?
q2.a: No. It is not a government system and its results are not official land records. It has no connection to any land office.

q3.q: Which land records does it contain?
q3.a: Only invented parcels, owners and documents created for the demo. See the Data sources page for the full list.

q4.q: How do I check a plot?
q4.a: Choose "Verify land", pick the district and upazila, then enter the mouza, khatian and dag number. You see the recorded details, history and risk indicators.

q5.q: What does the risk level mean?
q5.a: It counts fixed consistency rules that did not match, for example a seller who is not the recorded owner. It points a reviewer to look closer; it is not a finding of fraud.

q6.q: Can I rely on it before buying land?
q6.a: No. Use it only to learn what a check can show. Before any purchase, get official verification from the relevant authority and advice from a qualified lawyer.

q7.q: Why does every document need human review?
q7.a: Text read from a scan can be wrong, especially in Bangla handwriting or poor images. An officer must confirm the extracted fields before a record is approved.

q8.a: No for the public pages: checking a copy, tracking a mutation, the tools and the map overview. Officers and reviewers sign in to work on records.

q9.q: How do I change the language or text size?
q9.a: Use the language switch and the text-size buttons in the top bar. Your choice is remembered in this browser.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.purpose: What we have built in so far, what is still weak, and how to tell us.

s1.title: What is in place
s1.body: We aim to meet WCAG 2.1 level AA. These are the features you can use today:

items.i1: Bangla first, with English one click away
items.i2: Text-size buttons and a light or dark theme in the top bar
items.i3: Full keyboard use, a visible focus ring and a skip-to-content link
items.i4: Touch targets of at least 44 px
items.i5: Status shown by icon and text, never by colour alone

s2.title: Known gaps
s2.body: This is a student demo and has not had a full audit with assistive technology. Known gaps:

items.i1: The interactive map is mainly visual; the place menu and search give the same places as text
items.i2: Charts have text summaries nearby but not full data tables everywhere
items.i3: Bangla text from scanned documents may be misread by OCR
items.i4: PDF reports have not been tested with screen readers

s3.title: Tell us about a problem
s3.body: If something does not work for you, email support@landshield.demo with the page address and what happened. This is a demo address with no guaranteed reply time.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.purpose: What this demo stores about you and why.

s1.title: What we store
s1.body: Public pages need no account and do not ask for personal details. Signed-in staff accounts and their work create these records:

items.i1: Account: name, email address, role and preferred language
items.i2: Documents an officer uploads and the fields extracted from them
items.i3: An audit log of who did what, in which role, and when

s2.title: Browser storage
s2.body: We keep only what the site needs to work:

items.i1: Your theme, text size and language
items.i2: A flag that you signed in on this browser, and a sign-in cookie that scripts cannot read

s3.title: Third parties
s3.body: The map loads background tiles from OpenStreetMap, so that service can see your IP address and the area you view. Nothing else is sent to other companies.

s4.title: Demo data
s4.body: All parcels, owners and documents are synthetic. Do not upload real documents or real personal data. The hosted demo may be reset at any time, which deletes everything stored in it.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.purpose: The conditions for using this demonstration.

s1.title: Demonstration only
s1.body: LandShield BD is a prototype built on synthetic data. It is not a government system and does not create, change or certify any real land record.

s2.title: Please do not
s2.body: Use of the site is at your own risk. You agree not to:

items.i1: Rely on a result as legal proof of ownership or title
items.i2: Upload real personal or confidential documents
items.i3: Scrape, overload or probe the service or its data
items.i4: Try to bypass sign-in, roles or rate limits

s3.title: No legal advice
s3.body: Risk indicators and checks help a person look closer. They are not a legal opinion. Consult the relevant authority or a qualified lawyer before acting on a land transaction.

s4.title: Licence and warranty
s4.body: The source code is released under the MIT licence. Third-party data and fonts keep their own licences. The service is provided as is, without any warranty.

dataSources.title: Data sources
dataSources.purpose: Where every dataset in this demo comes from.

s1.title: Land records
s1.body: All land, deed and person records are synthetic and invented for this demo. No khatian, deed, owner or plot data was read from any government land-record system.

s2.title: Open data we use
s2.body: Third-party data is simplified and not official:

items.i1: Division, district and upazila boundaries: geoBoundaries (CC BY 4.0) through the bangladesh-geojson project (ODbL)
items.i3: Fonts: GNU FreeSans for generated PDFs

s3.title: Government portals
s3.body: The app and its scripts do not contact any government portal. An earlier version held data collected from such portals; it was removed and nothing from them remains.

s4.title: Tools that read documents
s4.body: Text is read from uploads by Tesseract OCR. An optional AI model can help parse fields when it is switched on. In every case a human reviews the result before approval.

items.i2: Claude by Anthropic (optional, off unless a key is set)
